Independent geometric reconstruction: let E and O be the two parity simplices and take the height equal to total odd barycentric weight. At height 1/2 the middle level L is the polyhedral complex of products Δ(S)×Δ(T) for nonempty even S, odd T, with all cross distances three. Complementing the odd labels alone identifies that bipartite relation with the ordinary cube graph and commutes with the original involution. Normalizing the two weight sets separately identifies the whole realization with the double mapping cylinder L→|E|, L→|O|. The involution preserves height; the two endpoint simplex quotients are contractible (radial contraction to invariant barycenters). Thus the ordinary quotient is homotopy equivalent to the suspension of L/C₂.

In the cube graph two distinct vertices on one side have two common neighbors precisely at distance two, and no three vertices on one side have two common neighbors. Thus L is formed by one star simplex per vertex of the cube (one side of the product a singleton), intersecting only at edge-points, plus one square per cubical square. Each star simplex may be replaced by the tree joining its barycenter to its edge-points, relative to those points. The sides of each attaching square then become the two-spoke paths between edge-points, since those paths are homotopic relative to their endpoints inside the corresponding simplex. These replacements and attaching homotopies can be made in involution pairs; equivalently make them in the quotient. This identifies L/C₂ up to homotopy with the antipodal quotient of the subdivided cubical 2-skeleton. That skeleton is simply connected since adjoining the higher-dimensional cells yields the full cube; its antipodal action is free. The quotient has π₁=C₂ and Euler characteristic (16−32+24)/2=4, so rank H₂=3. Dyer–Sieradski gives M(Z/2,1)∨3S² for this auxiliary two-complex. Suspending gives M(Z/2,2)∨3S³ for the actual quotient.
correctness.rationale: The fixed set is exactly two tetrahedra: an invariant support is a union of opposite pairs, and opposite pairs of different parity cannot coexist since the cross distances are 1 and 3. The frozen proof correctly distinguishes orbit cells after removing inversions, geometric free-facet removal, and purely algebraic integral chain contraction. In its quotient Δ-complex, a facet occurring once in the attaching boundary of its unique maximal coface permits a deformation of the characteristic simplex onto the other facets, relative to them; this descends even if other boundary faces have identifications. A unit matrix coefficient alone would not establish that. The final three-dimensional argument is sound: a simply connected 2-skeleton is a wedge of S² by Hurewicz and Whitehead, the 3-cell attachments are vectors in π₂, and unimodular basis changes are realized by self-equivalences of the domain and target sphere wedges of the attaching map. Thus the Smith factor two and three excess 3-cells give the claimed wedge. An independent proof of the homotopy conclusion is given in the evidence below; it does not rely on the transcript of the large collapse or integer computation.
residual_risks: These are exact finite and geometric verifications, not formal proof-assistant certification or a result for other cubes or subgroups.

value.rationale: Bit complement is the canonical central involution on the four-cube, with real fixed points in its independence complex. Its ordinary geometric quotient is a natural object already motivated by the contrast with the free Rips action and with the upstairs rational character. Identifying the degree-two Moore summand and the entire three-dimensional splitting is substantive integral information unavailable from a rational rank calculation; the small-dimensional quotient model gives a precise comparison for other cubical actions without making a generalization claim.
residual_risks: Value is for this exact nonfree quotient, not a prediction or theorem for larger cubes.
